sourceInformation.source: UFO! (Odyssey2, 1981), Ed Averett; Europe: Satellite Attack / Videopac 34
sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript/Canvas2D/Web Audio; my-3D2dge v0.89.1 (8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691), AI Hub session client v1.4.0 (35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869); esbuild 0.25.12 build-only
sourceInformation.artDirection: Native procedural pixel art with shaded volume, emissive accents and orbital charts
sourceInformation.animation: Native 120 Hz engine clock, tween/easing, Path, and procedural banking, orbital lights, shield/fusion/chain/boss motion
sourceInformation.audio: Original native chip-synth music, effects and code-generated gibberish; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: 1–2-player AI Hub shared-world authoritative co-op with prediction/interpolation; standalone simultaneous couch co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Unrestricted headless checks: deterministic legal-input complete missions/replay, co-op rescue/survivor victory, emulated pad/touch, Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, offline native audio, official Hub harness and two-page lossy gameplay. No physical devices, real internet session or human listener.
sourceInformation.research: Original UFO! manual and archival record/reviews, gameplay and regional box images inspected; audiovisual recording access failed, so exact historical audio is unknown. Evidence matrix in docs/research.md.

testingFeedback: Eight defects were caught by automated or visual testing and fixed; additional integration-review corrections are recorded in docs/issues.md.
Two critical defects were fixed overall: native boot-option scene blocking (found by testing), and paused shared-world authority (found by review).
The canonical full-mission legal-input playthrough and exact replay proved all combat interactions, every boss phase, extraction and victory without debug shortcuts.
Static string-presence packaging checks gave less behavioral evidence than input-driven journeys; they remain useful for metadata and client placement.
engineFeedback: Native pixel primitives, hue-shifted palette ramps, depth-sorted art and a complete controller/settings/synth foundation.

Yes. The documented boot:false route retained the engine booting flag and intercepted scene changes; ordinary scene startup fixed it. An initial overlay also obscured actors until moved to native decals.
The authoritative shield, collision, chain, encounter and simultaneous co-op simulation, plus replay and Hub state replication.
Keeping a fixed authoritative arena and clear native art across changing device shapes while separating presentation from multiplayer authority.
none; the vendored engine and released Hub client are unmodified. Game-specific systems extend their public APIs.
Provide a simultaneous shared-world arcade starter with authority-aware pause and an explicit validated viewport transform.
promptFeedback: Concrete mechanical pillars, source boundaries and end-to-end verification requirements made the intended game clear.
The engine starter uses viewport-derived arena bounds and alternating arcade players; the authored game requires fixed bounds and simultaneous pilots, so those defaults needed explicit replacement.
Integrating deterministic shield and chain combat with controller/touch menus and correct remote authority across the entire mission.
Prioritize the acceptance checks and put the final delivery naming and shared simulation contract together in one concise handoff.

aiHub.name: UFOh Orbit
aiHub.tagline: One shot. No shield. Your move.
aiHub.description: Pilot an overconfident saucer through four machinery-filled sectors. Spend your shield to shoot, ram with a ready ring, and spark cascades with a wingmate.
aiHub.controls: Left stick/WASD move; right stick/mouse aim; R2/Space/click fire; Options/Esc pause; invisible twin touch sticks.
